Let’s check the statement:  
"na won the lifetime achievement only after the year 1998."

First, "na" means "not applicable" or "no award given" in this table, so it’s not a winner’s name.  
The statement says "na won the lifetime achievement" — but "na" is not a person, it’s a placeholder for no award.  
So literally, "na" never "won" any award; it just appears in the table when no award was given.

Looking at the "lifetime achievement" column:  
- 1996: Jon Cleary (not na)  
- 1997: Alan Yates (not na)  
- 1998: na  
- 1999: Peter Corris (not na)  
- 2000: na  
- 2011: na  
So "na" appears in lifetime achievement in 1998, 2000, 2011, etc.  

The statement says "na won … only after the year 1998."  
"Only after 1998" means every occurrence of na in that column must be in years > 1998, and none in 1998 or earlier.  
But 1998 itself has na, which is not after 1998 (it’s in 1998).  
So the statement is false.

Final Answer: No
